content.title: Cardinals' Opening Day win ignites downtown St. Louis in sports-filled weekend
content.text: St. Louis basked in Opening Day glory as Cardinals fans filled downtown streets to celebrate a victory that kicks off a pivotal sports weekend. ST. LOUIS — Downtown St. Louis was transformed into a sea of red Thursday as fans poured out of Busch Stadium, celebrating a season-opening victory that served as the centerpiece for a major weekend in St. Louis sports. The Cardinals’ win over the Tampa Bay Rays kicked off a high-energy stretch for the city, which is also set to host St. Louis Blues hockey games and the home opener for the UFL’s St. Louis Battlehawks. For those gathered at the corner of Clark Avenue and Eighth Street, however, the day was defined by the return of a singular local obsession. “Fantastic. With all the former players that were down there and the crowd, the atmosphere today, even though it was 94 in March, it was a fantastic day,” fan David Lawshe remarked as the crowd dispersed into the downtown streets. Opening Day remains an unofficial holiday in St. Louis, drawing generations of families to the ballpark. For some, the commitment to being present for the first pitch involves significant travel. “Every year this is what I look forward to every year. This is the 25th in a row me and my dad have been to so it's tradition family tradition. I actually flew here from Denver yesterday as I moved to Colorado a month ago. But we had to keep it going and opening day is always the best,” a longtime fan Trey Weishar said. The festivities included the traditional pre-game ceremonies, featuring the Budweiser Clydesdales and a procession of the franchise's legendary figures. “It was definitely an experience. All the pre-stuff, all the horses, seeing all the Hall of Fame members. Oh my gosh. It was amazing,” Collin Walker said. While the pageantry provided the backdrop, the performance of a roster featuring several new faces provided the substance. Despite external skepticism regarding the team’s trajectory, those in the stands expressed an early-season optimism. “I think people are down on the Cardinals and they shouldn't be. It's a rebuilding year and they showed amazing talent. JJ was amazing and I think we have to believe,” fan Suzan Knese noted, following the win. Security and stadium logistics were also at the forefront of the day’s operations. Attendees reported a smooth experience despite the large capacity crowd. “I thought safety was fine. The crowds didn't seem, I don't know, too crowded. You could get in the stadium and do things that you needed to do,” Lawshe said. As the city prepares for a weekend of further competition, including the remainder of the series against the Rays on Saturday and Sunday, the sentiment downtown remained one of defiant hope. “I think we're going to shock a lot of people this year, honestly. But baseball, we're a baseball city. So, it's important to everyone here,” Weishar said.
